blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The idea of a Constituent Assembly for India was first put forward by M.N. Roy in 1934.
The Constituent Assembly held its first historic meeting on December 9, 1946.
Jawaharlal Nehru moved the groundbreaking Objectives Resolution on December 13, 1946.
The Drafting Committee was appointed on August 29, 1947, under the chairmanship of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
The Constitution was formally adopted on November 26, 1949, and fully enforced on January 26, 1950.
INTRODUCTION

blocks.content: The framing of the Indian Constitution is one of the most remarkable events in the political history of India. The Constitution was not created suddenly; rather, it was the result of years of deliberations, debates, and discussions conducted by the Constituent Assembly.

The makers of the Constitution carefully studied the constitutions of various countries and adopted the best features suitable to Indian conditions. The Constitution reflects the ideals of democracy, justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
The idea of a Constituent Assembly was first proposed by M. N. Roy in 1934. Later, the Indian National Congress officially demanded the formation of a Constituent Assembly in 1935.
The British Government accepted this demand in principle through the August Offer (1940) and finally implemented it through the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.
The Constituent Assembly was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946. Total Members – 389

items:
• 292 members from British Indian Provinces
  • 93 members from Princely States
  • 4 members from Chief Commissioner‟s Provinces
292 members from British Indian Provinces
93 members from Princely States
4 members from Chief Commissioner‟s Provinces

blocks.content: Members were elected indirectly by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies using proportional representation.

blocks.content: The Constituent Assembly began its work in a democratic and representative manner.
The Objectives Resolution was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946. It laid down the philosophy and ideals of the Constitution.

items:
• India to be a Sovereign State
  • Justice – social, economic and political
  • Liberty of thought, expression, belief and worship
  • Equality of status and opportunity
  • Fraternity and unity of the nation

D. P. Khaitan (later replaced by T. T. Krishnamachari) The committee prepared the final draft of the Constitution.
Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha served as the temporary President during the first meeting before Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as permanent President.
The Objectives Resolution introduced by Nehru formed the foundational source of the Preamble of India.
January 26 was specifically chosen for enforcement to commemorate the declaration of Purna Swaraj in 1930.

blocks.content: The framing of the Indian Constitution was a historic achievement. The Constituent Assembly worked with dedication, wisdom and foresight to frame a Constitution suitable for a diverse country like India. The Constitution continues to guide the nation as the supreme law of the land.
